text: Let $f:\mathrm{ℝ}-\{5\}\to \mathrm{ℝ}$ be defined as $f(x)=\dfrac{2x^{2}+3x-2}{x-5}$. Then $f$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Put $y=f(x)$: $2x^{2}+(3-y)x+(5y-2)=0$ ($x=5$ is never a root, since $50+15-2\neq 0$).

$y$ is attained only if the discriminant is non-negative: $(3-y)^{2}-8(5y-2)=y^{2}-46y+25\geq 0$.

For $y=23$ this is $-504<0$, so $23$ is not in the range and $f$ is not onto.

Also $f\left (\dfrac{1}{2}\right )=f(-2)=0$, so $f$ is not one-one.

text:
If the system of linear equations

$λx+y-z=-1$

$x-y-3z=2$

$-x+y+z=μ$

has infinitely many solutions, then the equation of the line passing through the points $(λ+2μ,2λ+μ)$ and $(1,λμ)$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For infinitely many solutions, $\Delta =\left |\begin{array}{lll} λ & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & -3 \\ -1 & 1 & 1 \end{array}\right |=2λ+2=0\Rightarrow λ=-1$.

With $λ=-1$: adding the first two equations gives $-4z=1$; adding the last two gives $-2z=2+μ$.

Consistency: $z=-\dfrac{1}{4}\Rightarrow 2+μ=\dfrac{1}{2}\Rightarrow μ=-\dfrac{3}{2}$.

Points: $(λ+2μ,2λ+μ)=\left (-4,-\dfrac{7}{2}\right )$ and $(1,λμ)=\left (1,\dfrac{3}{2}\right )$; slope $=\dfrac{\frac{3}{2}+\frac{7}{2}}{1+4}=1$.

Line: $y-\dfrac{3}{2}=x-1\Rightarrow 2x-2y=-1$.

text:
Let

$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \dfrac{\sin (ax+3x)+\sin x}{x}, & x<0 \\ 2, & x=0 \\ \dfrac{(x+6bx^{2})^{\frac{1}{3}}-x^{\frac{1}{3}}}{3x^{4/3}}, & x>0 \end{array} \right.$
be continuous at $x=0$. If $(1-k)f\left (\dfrac{7}{18}\right )=ab$, then $k$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\lim _{x\to 0^{-}}\dfrac{\sin (ax+3x)+\sin x}{x}=(a+3)+1=a+4=2\Rightarrow a=-2$.

For $x>0$: $f(x)=\dfrac{x^{1/3}\left [(1+6bx)^{1/3}-1\right ]}{3x^{4/3}}=\dfrac{(1+6bx)^{1/3}-1}{3x}$.

$\lim _{x\to 0^{+}}f(x)=\dfrac{1}{3}\cdot \dfrac{6b}{3}=\dfrac{2b}{3}=2\Rightarrow b=3$, so $ab=-6$.

$f\left (\dfrac{7}{18}\right )=\dfrac{(1+7)^{1/3}-1}{3\cdot \frac{7}{18}}=\dfrac{1}{7/6}=\dfrac{6}{7}$.

$(1-k)\cdot \dfrac{6}{7}=-6\Rightarrow 1-k=-7\Rightarrow k=8$.

text: Let $A_{k}=\int\limits _{kπ}^{(k+1)π}e^{-x}\sin xdx$, $k=0,1,2,\ldots ,20$. Then $\sum\limits _{k=0}^{20}|A_{k}|$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
By parts, $\int e^{-x}\sin xdx=-\dfrac{e^{-x}}{2}(\sin x+\cos x)$.

$A_{k}=-\dfrac{1}{2}\left [e^{-(k+1)π}\cos (k+1)π-e^{-kπ}\cos kπ\right ]=\dfrac{(-1)^{k}}{2}e^{-kπ}(1+e^{-π})$.

$|A_{k}|=\dfrac{1+e^{-π}}{2}e^{-kπ}$, a G.P. with ratio $e^{-π}$.

$\sum\limits _{k=0}^{20}|A_{k}|=\dfrac{1+e^{-π}}{2}\cdot \dfrac{1-e^{-21π}}{1-e^{-π}}=\dfrac{1}{2}\left (\dfrac{e^{π}+1}{e^{π}-1}\right )\left (1-e^{-21π}\right )$.

text: If $y=y(x)$ satisfies the differential equation $xdy+\left (x\tan \left (\dfrac{y}{x}\right )-y\right )dx=0$, $x>0$, and $y(1)=\dfrac{π}{2}$, then a value of $y(\sqrt{2})$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y}{x}-\tan \dfrac{y}{x}$ (homogeneous). Put $y=vx$: $v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=v-\tan v$.

$\cot v\qquad dv=-\dfrac{dx}{x}\Rightarrow \ln |\sin v|=-\ln x+c\Rightarrow \sin \dfrac{y}{x}=\dfrac{C}{x}$.

$y(1)=\dfrac{π}{2}\Rightarrow C=1$, so $x\sin \dfrac{y}{x}=1$.

At $x=\sqrt{2}$: $\sin \dfrac{y}{\sqrt{2}}=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\Rightarrow \dfrac{y}{\sqrt{2}}=\dfrac{π}{4}$ or $\dfrac{3π}{4}$.

So $y(\sqrt{2})=\dfrac{π}{2\sqrt{2}}$ or $\dfrac{3π}{2\sqrt{2}}$; the value $\dfrac{3π}{2\sqrt{2}}$ is among the options.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: Let the area enclosed by the solution curve $y=y(x)$ of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{x-2}{y-b}=2$, $b>0$, $y(5)=0$ is $13π$. Let $y=y(x)$ intersect the $y$-axis at the points $P$ and $Q$. If the tangents to $y=y(x)$ at $P$ and $Q$ meet at $T$, then the area of $\Delta PTQ$ is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An enclosed area needs a closed curve, so the equation is read as $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{x-2}{y-b}=0$, i.e. $(y-b)dy+(x-2)dx=0$.

Integrating: $(x-2)^{2}+(y-b)^{2}=r^{2}$, a circle with centre $(2,b)$; $πr^{2}=13π\Rightarrow r^{2}=13$.

$y(5)=0$: $9+b^{2}=13\Rightarrow b=2$ $(b>0)$.

On $x=0$: $(y-2)^{2}=9\Rightarrow P(0,5)$, $Q(0,-1)$.

Tangent at $P$: $-2(x-2)+3(y-2)=13$, i.e. $-2x+3y=15$. By symmetry $T$ lies on $y=2$, so $T\left (-\dfrac{9}{2},2\right )$.

Area of $\Delta PTQ=\dfrac{1}{2}\times PQ\times \dfrac{9}{2}=\dfrac{1}{2}\times 6\times \dfrac{9}{2}=13.5$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Ellipse: $c^{2}=25-9=16$, foci $(\pm 4,0)$. Hyperbola: $a^{2}+12=16\Rightarrow a^{2}=4$; with $a=2$ the point is $(2,3)$.

Required hyperbola: $\dfrac{y^{2}}{B^{2}}-\dfrac{x^{2}}{A^{2}}=1$ with $A^{2}+B^{2}=10$.

Through $(2,3)$: $\dfrac{9}{B^{2}}-\dfrac{4}{10-B^{2}}=1\Rightarrow B^{4}-23B^{2}+90=0\Rightarrow B^{2}=5$ (since $B^{2}<10$).

$e=\dfrac{\sqrt{10}}{B}=\dfrac{\sqrt{10}}{\sqrt{5}}=\sqrt{2}$.

If the mean and median of the data

$x0-1010-2020-3030-4040-50f362xy\sum f=20$
are equal, then $xy^{2}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$3+6+2+x+y=20\Rightarrow x+y=9$.

Cumulative frequencies $3,9,11,\ldots$; $\dfrac{N}{2}=10$, so the median class is $20-30$.

Median $=20+\dfrac{10-9}{2}\times 10=25$.

Mean $=\dfrac{5(3)+15(6)+25(2)+35x+45y}{20}=25\Rightarrow 35x+45y=345\Rightarrow 7x+9y=69$.

With $x+y=9$: $x=6$, $y=3$, so $xy^{2}=6\times 9=54$.

text: The number of solutions of the equation $|x^{2}+3x+2|+|x+5|-2=0$, $x\in \mathrm{ℝ}$, is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$|x^{2}+3x+2|+|x+5|=2$ needs $|x+5|\leq 2$, i.e. $-7\leq x\leq -3$.

On $[-7,-3]$, $x^{2}+3x+2=(x+1)(x+2)\geq 2$, so the left side is $x^{2}+3x+2+|x+5|$.

For $-5\leq x\leq -3$: $x^{2}+4x+7=(x+2)^{2}+3\geq 4$; for $-7\leq x\leq -5$: $x^{2}+2x-3=(x+1)^{2}-4\geq 12$.

So the left side is always at least $4>2$, and the equation has no real solution.

Number of solutions $=0$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: The number of integral values of $b$ for which $2x^{3}-3x^{2}-12x+b=0$ has three distinct real roots is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $f(x)=2x^{3}-3x^{2}-12x$; the equation is $f(x)=-b$.

$f^{'}(x)=6x^{2}-6x-12=6(x-2)(x+1)$: local maximum $f(-1)=7$, local minimum $f(2)=-20$.

Three distinct real roots $⟺-20<-b<7⟺-7<b<20$.

Integers $b=-6,-5,\ldots ,19$: $26$ values.

text:
An air duct is made of a thick metallic sheet. The duct is open from front and back. Its cross-section is a trapezium of base angles $60^{\circ }$ and area $1.5\mathrm{m}^{2}$. Its length is $1\mathrm{m}$. (see the figure). If its height $x=x_{0}$ (in metres) so that the area of the metallic sheet used for its construction is minimum, then $16(x_{0})^{4}$ is equal to $________$.


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the longer parallel side be $b$; the shorter one is $b-2x\cot 60^{\circ }=b-\dfrac{2x}{\sqrt{3}}$ and each slant side is $\dfrac{x}{\sin 60^{\circ }}=\dfrac{2x}{\sqrt{3}}$.

Area: $\left (b-\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{3}}\right )x=\dfrac{3}{2}\Rightarrow b=\dfrac{3}{2x}+\dfrac{x}{\sqrt{3}}$.

Sheet area $S=(\text{perimeter})\times 1=2b-\dfrac{2x}{\sqrt{3}}+\dfrac{4x}{\sqrt{3}}=\dfrac{3}{x}+\dfrac{4x}{\sqrt{3}}$.

$\dfrac{dS}{dx}=-\dfrac{3}{x^{2}}+\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{3}}=0\Rightarrow x_{0}^{2}=\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{4}$, and $\dfrac{d^{2}S}{dx^{2}}=\dfrac{6}{x^{3}}>0$ (minimum).

$16x_{0}^{4}=16\times \dfrac{27}{16}=27$.

text: If the area enclosed by the curves $y=x^{2}$, $y^{3}=x$, $x=-1$ and $y=x^{2}$, $y^{3}=x$, $x=1$, above the line $x=2y$ is $\dfrac{n}{n+1}$, then $n$ is equal to $______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $-1\leq x\leq 0$ the region lies between $y=x^{2}$ (above) and $y=x^{1/3}$ (below), and the line $y=\dfrac{x}{2}$ lies above $y=x^{1/3}$ there.

Part above the line: $\int\limits _{-1}^{0}\left (x^{2}-\dfrac{x}{2}\right )dx=\dfrac{1}{3}+\dfrac{1}{4}=\dfrac{7}{12}$.

For $0\leq x\leq 1$ the region is $x^{2}\leq y\leq x^{1/3}$; the line $y=\dfrac{x}{2}$ meets $y=x^{2}$ at $x=\dfrac{1}{2}$.

Part above the line: $\int\limits _{0}^{1}x^{1/3}dx-\int\limits _{0}^{1/2}\dfrac{x}{2}dx-\int\limits _{1/2}^{1}x^{2}dx=\dfrac{3}{4}-\dfrac{1}{16}-\dfrac{7}{24}=\dfrac{19}{48}$.

Total $=\dfrac{7}{12}+\dfrac{19}{48}=\dfrac{47}{48}=\dfrac{n}{n+1}\Rightarrow n=47$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: Let $A(0,a+2)$, $B(0,a)$, $C(-2,0)$ and $D(2,0)$ be four points and the lines $AD$ and $BC$ intersect at $P(x,y)$. If the locus of $P$ is the curve $f(x,y)=0$ and the tangent at the point $(4,γ)$ on this curve is $\dfrac{x}{α}+\dfrac{y}{β}=1$, then $α(β-γ)$ is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)
tags: straight lines and pair of straight lines

solution.body:
$AD$: $\dfrac{x}{2}+\dfrac{y}{a+2}=1\Rightarrow a+2=\dfrac{2y}{2-x}$; $BC$: $-\dfrac{x}{2}+\dfrac{y}{a}=1\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{2y}{2+x}$.

Subtracting: $2=\dfrac{2y}{2-x}-\dfrac{2y}{2+x}=\dfrac{4xy}{4-x^{2}}\Rightarrow$ locus $x^{2}+2xy-4=0$.

$(4,γ)$ lies on it: $16+8γ-4=0\Rightarrow γ=-\dfrac{3}{2}$.

Tangent at $\left (4,-\dfrac{3}{2}\right )$: $4x+\left (-\dfrac{3}{2}x+4y\right )-4=0\Rightarrow 5x+8y=8\Rightarrow \dfrac{x}{8/5}+\dfrac{y}{1}=1$.

$α=\dfrac{8}{5}$, $β=1$: $α(β-γ)=\dfrac{8}{5}\times \dfrac{5}{2}=4$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: Let $L_{1}$ be a line in the $yz$-plane with $y$ and $z$ intercepts $\dfrac{1}{4}$ and $\dfrac{1}{C}$ $(C>0)$ respectively. Let $L_{2}$ be the line in the $xz$-plane with $x$ and $z$ intercepts $\dfrac{1}{3}$ and $-\dfrac{1}{C}$ respectively. If the shortest distance between $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$ is $\dfrac{1}{5}$, then $C^{2}$ is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$L_{1}$ passes through $\left (0,\frac{1}{4},0\right )$ and $\left (0,0,\frac{1}{C}\right )$: direction $⃗{d}_{1}=(0,-C,4)$.

$L_{2}$ passes through $\left (\frac{1}{3},0,0\right )$ and $\left (0,0,-\frac{1}{C}\right )$: direction $⃗{d}_{2}=(C,0,3)$.

$⃗{d}_{1}\times ⃗{d}_{2}=(-3C,4C,C^{2})$; with the joining vector $\left (\frac{1}{3},-\frac{1}{4},0\right )$ the dot product is $-C-C=-2C$.

Shortest distance $=\dfrac{2C}{\sqrt{25C^{2}+C^{4}}}=\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{25+C^{2}}}=\dfrac{1}{5}$.

$25+C^{2}=100\Rightarrow C^{2}=75$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: Let $OABC$ be a parallelogram, $O$ be the origin, $A(2,4,-5)$ and $C(b,2,3)$. If $P(a,a,a)$ and $Q(9-a^{2},3,a-1)$, $a\in \mathrm{ℕ}$, are two points such that the projection of $OP\leftarrow$ on $OB\leftarrow$ is 2 and $OQ\leftarrow$ makes acute angles with all three co-ordinate axes, then $\left |OB\leftarrow \right |^{2}+\left |AC\leftarrow \right |^{2}$ is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$OQ\leftarrow$ makes acute angles with all axes: $9-a^{2}>0$ and $a-1>0$; with $a\in \mathrm{ℕ}$ this gives $a=2$, so $P(2,2,2)$.

$OB\leftarrow =OA\leftarrow +OC\leftarrow =(b+2,6,-2)$.

Projection: $\dfrac{2(b+2)+12-4}{\sqrt{(b+2)^{2}+40}}=2\Rightarrow b+6=\sqrt{(b+2)^{2}+40}$.

$b^{2}+12b+36=b^{2}+4b+44\Rightarrow b=1$, so $OB\leftarrow =(3,6,-2)$ and $AC\leftarrow =(-1,-2,8)$.

$\left |OB\leftarrow \right |^{2}+\left |AC\leftarrow \right |^{2}=49+69=118$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: The probability distribution of a random variable $X$ is $P(X=i)=\dfrac{1}{2^{i}}$, $i=1,2,3,\ldots$ The variance of $X$ is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Using $\sum\limits _{i\geq 1}ix^{i}=\dfrac{x}{(1-x)^{2}}$ and $\sum\limits _{i\geq 1}i^{2}x^{i}=\dfrac{x(1+x)}{(1-x)^{3}}$ at $x=\dfrac{1}{2}$:

$E(X)=\sum\limits _{i\geq 1}\dfrac{i}{2^{i}}=2$ and $E(X^{2})=\sum\limits _{i\geq 1}\dfrac{i^{2}}{2^{i}}=6$.

$\mathrm{Var}(X)=E(X^{2})-[E(X)]^{2}=6-4=2$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text:
Let $S=\left \{θ\in [0,2π]-\left \{\dfrac{π}{2},\dfrac{3π}{2}\right \}:\sin ^{-1}(\sin θ)+\cos ^{-1}(\cos θ)+\tan ^{-1}(\tan θ)=\dfrac{4π}{5}\right \}$.

Then $\dfrac{30}{π}\sum\limits _{θ\in S}θ$ is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$θ\in \left [0,\frac{π}{2}\right )$: sum $=θ+θ+θ=3θ=\dfrac{4π}{5}\Rightarrow θ=\dfrac{4π}{15}$ (valid).

$θ\in \left (\frac{π}{2},π\right ]$: sum $=(π-θ)+θ+(θ-π)=θ\Rightarrow θ=\dfrac{4π}{5}$ (valid).

$θ\in \left (π,\frac{3π}{2}\right )$: sum $=(π-θ)+(2π-θ)+(θ-π)=2π-θ\Rightarrow θ=\dfrac{6π}{5}$ (valid).

$θ\in \left (\frac{3π}{2},2π\right ]$: sum $=(θ-2π)+(2π-θ)+(θ-2π)=θ-2π\leq 0$: no solution.

$\dfrac{30}{π}\sum\limits _{θ\in S}θ=\dfrac{30}{π}\cdot \dfrac{(4+12+18)π}{15}=68$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift
